1#א: By way of cooking — to exclude salting or pickling. And roasting has opinions; see Peleti that one should be stringent.
1#ב: Cooking — see Peleti: if one cooked seven olives of milk with one olive of meat, even though not as people cook, as Rashi wrote — nevertheless forbidden for benefit from the Torah.
1#ג: All meat — Peri Chadash's view: if not cooked as food fit for Ben Drusai it is not forbidden from the Torah, for we say: in which cooking did they speak? In cooking that others eat — and that is Ben Drusai; see Peleti that I wrote it is not so, rather all that comes to heat is d'oraisa forbidden — see there.
1#ד: Permitted. And all forbidden for benefit must be buried and one may not burn it — if buried its ash is forbidden; if burned its ash is permitted; and one may throw it in a privy and the like — see what I wrote in Peleti.
3#א: Pure domestic animal — see what I wrote in Peleti reconciling Rambam's words.
3#ב: And impure domestic animal meat — Bach's view: rabbinically forbidden because of basar b'chalav, and practical difference regarding piece becoming nevelah; and there is another difference. Only Acharonim wondered why the Sages decreed thus since in any case it is forbidden because of impure meat — where is this hinted in the Sages' words? And it is possible the tanna teaches: pure domestic meat in impure milk is permitted in cooking and benefit — that 'permitted in cooking and benefit' is superfluous; it should have said merely 'permitted' — and it is clear it does not refer to eating; for when one eats an impure thing we need precision that in eating it is forbidden because of basar b'chalav.
3#ג: Since it is only rabbinic — Shach and Taz disagree; and many rabbinic prohibitions they decreed because of marit ayin, and there was no need to search, for this law we learn from blood placed in a vessel, etc.; and blood cooked is rabbinic — nevertheless Peri Chadash agreed to permit, for one does not compare rabbinic decrees to each other. And I add: it is not milk but fruit juice — almond milk; because it resembles milk in appearance it is forbidden. And red wine did not change though it resembles blood — and so the Sages forbade woman's milk and fish blood which is blood, and actual milk — see Peleti.
4#_: All the more so, etc. — Acharonim wrote the essence of marit ayin is in eating and not in cooking; see what I wrote in Peleti — another distinction; see there where I expanded in place of R' Yehudah HaChasid on cooking fowl meat in milk — where does marit ayin go?
5#א: Even though entangled in sinews, etc. — although above siman 86 poskim hold when he struck the chicken on its tail and it laid eggs forbidden because of eiver min ha'chai — that is eiver min ha'chai, for although not called meat, nevertheless eiver min ha'chai applies — it does not depend whether called meat, for this draws from the living; but regarding basar b'chalav what of it that entangled in sinews — nevertheless it is not called basar b'chalav; see what I wrote in Peleti on Shach and Peri Chadash.
5#ב: Behold this — and Rashbam's view: as long as the outer shell is not hard, forbidden to cook it in milk; and the sage wrote one should practice so l'chatchila; see Shach; see what I wrote in Peleti reconciling Rashbam's words so they do not contradict the Gemara and are resolved in Tosafot.
5#ג: But if it has only, etc. — Shach wrote even if not entangled in sinews it is forbidden; see Peleti that in Torat HaBayit it does not appear so; and although one may reject — from where do we forbid with great stringency in a rabbinic prohibition?
6#א: Smoked, etc. — Peri Chadash wrote: since it is in Yerushalmi tractate Shabbat that smoked is cooking for Shabbat, so too for basar b'chalav; see Peleti that one may reject, for in basar b'chalav we require a way of cooking.
6#ב: Because of basar b'chalav — it appears therefore for blood one would receive lashes for eating, and this is Rambam's wording who holds blood cooked one violates; but per what we hold blood cooked is rabbinic — likewise for blood there is none.
6#ג: Forbidden to stoke, etc. — although it is nevelah meat and basar b'chalav does not apply in cooking — nevertheless it applies; and so Rambam; see Peleti where I discussed one who cooks nevelah in milk whether forbidden for benefit; see there resolving challenges on Rambam and Tosafot Shevuot; and I explained Rambam's wording in his commentary on the Mishnah why it is not called basar b'chalav because of prohibition of benefit — additional prohibition — see there.
6#ד: To stoke — Shach wrote: and the same applies to other vessels in which they cook — forbidden to stoke when there is absorbed meat and milk, and the absorbed becomes cooked; and it is only a mere stringency — end; see what I wrote in Peleti whether absorbed in a vessel is cooking for basar b'chalav; also whether cooking after cooking applies in basar b'chalav.
6#ה: Forbidden for benefit — meaning boiling water and yad soledes bo; and that we do not forbid because of telling a gentile — rabbinic shevut in other prohibitions — that is not explicit; and even for basar b'chalav telling a gentile is shevut — meaning we are not certain there are sixty in the water against the prohibition, only a d'oraisa doubt to be stringent; but regarding shevut, rabbinic doubt is lenient.
6#ו: That one may not use them — and it is difficult: since there is in that ash concern for mixture of basar b'chalav, and you forbid use — how do they permit placing kiln ash in the pot? Behold it cooks basar b'chalav; and if there is no concern for cooking, there is also no concern for benefit to permit what I wrote in Peleti; and in resolving many challenges of Tzitz Eliezer — when is noten taam lifgam permitted and when forbidden; see there what I wrote when noten taam lifgam is permitted and when forbidden, and many challenges are resolved.
9#_: Even when clear — which is like digested; and some forbid — he holds when clear it is not like digested.
10#א: Forbidden to set rennet in it — per Mechaber everything is forbidden l'chatchila.
10#ב: Until there are sixty — and that a setting agent even in a thousand is not nullified; and the stomach piece becoming nevelah — Shach explained they were not so stringent in salting that it becomes nevelah, and even in a thousand not nullified; and from what I wrote in Peleti — two ways: either this source is from Tur, or Tur does not hold at all that setting is not nullified; and Orach Chaim wrote siman 347: since it stands in existence — meaning to nullify — practical difference in noten taam as first taste; but sixty is required; or here it is proven impossible to nullify in a thousand — proven from Gemara that one need not distinguish clear and dried; if so here you do not come to forbid because of setting agent, etc.; if so no distinction between dried and clear — and one walks as a fool in darkness — see there.
10#ג: It does not forbid — and that which it came is second taste permitting the first of prohibition — meat in stomach and stomach in milk; Shach wrote it is like excrement; and although strained — nevertheless mere water; if so still second taste permitting the first; per the reason: since it was not pickled a full day or in boiling there is no absorption at all unless he set rennet, for the action of setting is recognizable and acts like boiling; but here there is only second taste permitting the first — not recognizable and considered merely cold; and so I raised in Peleti whether they are boiling or pickling by itself; even when dried one may be stringent — second taste permitting the first to forbid; but when cold one may be lenient — see there.
10#ד: And congealed has the law of clear — Beit HaTaharah disagrees; see Peleti where I proved Tosafot's view is also thus; and if doubtful whether clear or dried we follow leniency; especially since dried is before you.
11#א: Meat taste — for us there is no tasting, only sixty.
11#ב: This meat — R' Yonatan of Gash's view: in Torat HaBayit it is permitted except cooking is forbidden by Torah; and this is not a way of cooking since there is no taste, only setting in a vessel; unlike setting in prohibition — Raavad's view: everywhere even setting requires sixty; only with gentiles they were stringent; but with Israel one may be lenient even setting in a prohibited item; and primary is Shulchan Aruch — they are Rambam's words.
11#ג: Permitted — meaning when the prohibition cannot set by itself; but if the prohibition can set by itself — not permitted; Shach.
